fields.label: Printer Name
fields.description: Free text — type the printer name EXACTLY as it appears on the cashier's local OS (Windows: 'EPSON TM-T88V', macOS: 'Kitchen-Star', CUPS: 'Kitchen_Printer'). For QZ Tray mode, this is what the browser sends to the local printer driver. For CUPS Direct mode, this is what CUPS uses to look up the queue.

fields.label: Description
fields.description: Optional. Where is this printer located? e.g. 'Bar station — behind the till' or 'Kitchen — food pass'.

fields.label: Disabled
fields.description: When checked, the POS will treat this printer as offline and fall back according to the POS Profile's Print Fallback Mode.

fields.label: CUPS Direct Settings (optional)
fields.description: Only required when your POS Profile's Print Mode is set to 'CUPS (Direct)'. For QZ Tray mode, leave these blank — QZ reads the printer directly from the cashier's browser OS.

fields.label: CUPS Server IP
fields.description: Hostname or IP of the CUPS server that hosts this printer. Only used when the POS Profile is in CUPS Direct mode.

fields.options: Heads-up: CUPS Direct mode requires the Frappe server to reach this CUPS server over the network AND the pycups Python package to be installed. On cloud-hosted Frappe deployments this is usually impossible because the server can't see the restaurant's local network. Use QZ Tray mode on the POS Profile instead — it runs in the cashier's browser and talks to the local printer directly.
